title: Mariposa Pharma cost reduction synthesis
body:
Executive summary:

This note summarizes a light-touch, customer-specific before/after analysis for Mariposa Pharmacy (customer has a med/clinical Q&A assistant and document search workflows). The objective: reduce monthly inference spend while preserving clinical answer quality and 95th-percentile latency targets. The recommendations combine model routing, quantized model variants, KV (prefix) caching for repeat sessions, conservative prompt compression, and targeted batching for embedding and long-context requests.

High-level headline: estimated run-rate savings of 48% (conservative) to 64% (aggressive) on inference compute and token costs. Net customer-facing risk is low if we adopt a staged rollout with evaluation gates.

Baseline (current) assumptions:
- Workload: 650k API calls / month across two main routes: "assistant-chat" (60% by volume, median input+output length 1.6k tokens) and "doc-search-embed+rerank" (40% by volume).
- Models: default large generator = open-70b (float16) for chat; short-chat uses 13B sometimes via customer routing rules; embeddings = base-embedding-v2.
- Deployment: Hosted API multi-region, no dedicated capacity, no persistent KV caching, default batching (minimal).
- Monthly spend snapshot (actual invoices + RW telemetry): total inference-related spend = $210,000; breakdown: model compute/GPU hours $150,000, token processing & per-request overhead $45,000, embedding egress/ops $15,000.
- Latency SLA: 95p target < 800ms for core chat queries (current 95p observed ~780ms).

Key cost drivers identified:
1) Heavy use of 70B for mid-length queries where a 13B/quantized-30B variant would suffice.
2) No KV/prefix reuse for clinical sessions — repeated context re-encoded on each request.
3) Low batching efficiency on embedding route: many small embedding calls (avg 3 vectors) leading to underutilized throughput.
4) No model variant selection based on prompt shape; all long-context flows default to the largest available model.

Recommended interventions (ordered by expected return / operational risk):
A) Model routing + fallback policy (low friction)
- Route short and medium prompts to 13B or quantized 30B variant; reserve 70B for genuinely long/high-importance flows.
- Configure automatic fallback to larger model only on quality regressions or explicit failure.
- Expected direct savings: 22% of current compute spend.

B) Kv/prefix caching for patient sessions (moderate effort)
- Enable prefix/KV caching for session-scoped contexts (typical clinical session has 3–7 exchanges). Cache warm-rate projected 65% after 2 weeks.
- Reduces repeated token throughput and reduces per-request latency for warmed sessions.
- Expected direct savings: 18% of compute/token spend; additional latency improvement for warmed sessions ~120–200ms.

C) Embedding batching + async aggregation (low effort)
- Introduce a short aggregation window (50–200ms) for bulk-upload batch embedding endpoint used by search ingestion and user uploads. For interactive embeddings keep immediate path.
- Expected direct savings on embedding spend: 40% on embedding GPU time and cheaper tokenization overheads; net monthly embedding spend reduced from $15k to ~$9k in conservative case.

D) Quantized model variants for 70B/30B (higher impact, operational testing)
- On-hosted and dedicated options, encourage customer to test int8/4-bit variant on a representative eval set. Expect per-token GPU time reduction 1.6–2.2x depending on format and hardware.
- Expected direct savings: incremental 10–18% assuming safe rollout (paired with canary and quality checks).

E) Prompt templating + aggressive prefix trimming (policy / product)
- Small behavioral change: convert chat system prompts into compressed templates and trim request context to necessary spans for long histories (e.g., last 3 exchanges + extracted patient fields).
- Expected token-level savings: ~5–8% across chat route.

Combined scenario math (conservative / likely / aggressive):
- Baseline monthly inference spend: $210,000

Conservative (safe rollout, partial adoption):
- Model routing: -22% of compute ($33k)
- KV cache: -18% of compute/token ($27k)
- Embedding batching: -40% of embed spend ($6k)
- Quantization: +5% reduction (partial) ($7k)
- Prompt templating: -6% ($9k)
- Net conservative savings: $82k => new monthly run-rate $128k => 39% reduction from baseline

Likely (full recommended stack, stable canaries):
- Model routing: -28% ($42k)
- KV cache: -22% ($33k)
- Embedding batching: -45% ($6.75k)
- Quantization: -12% ($18k)
- Prompt templating: -7% ($14.7k)
- Net likely savings: $113.45k => new monthly run-rate $96.55k => 54% reduction from baseline

Aggressive (dedicated + full quantization + capacity commitments):
- Additional savings from committed Dedicated pools (lower per-GPU cost) and deeper quantization + more aggressive batching: incremental 10–20% of remaining compute
- Net aggressive savings estimated 64% => run-rate ~$75.6k/month.

Operational considerations & risks:
- Quality regresses primarily at routing + quantization boundary. Mitigation: small eval set (100 representative clinical queries + 200 gold standard embeddings) used for A/B before route switch. Monitor: Rouge/EM-like metrics, human review for high-confidence adverse cases.
- Latency impacts: batching improves throughput but can increase p50 for some synchronous flows; mitigate by leaving critical interactive path unbatched and using short-window batching for background flows.
- Security/compliance: KV caching stores transient patient-derived context; requires encryption-at-rest and retention policy aligned to Mariposa's DPA — legal review required.

Implementation plan (8-week suggested timeline):
Week 0–1: align with Mariposa PM/infra, run a quick telemetry ingest to confirm workload mix and token distribution. Owner: Priya (PM).
Week 1–2: implement model routing rules in staging; run A/B with 5% traffic to quantized/13B variants. Owner: Ethan (engineer).
Week 2–4: enable KV caching for sessions under feature flag; collect warm-rate metrics and perf. Owner: Lin (SRE).
Week 3–5: enable embedding batching endpoints for background ingestion; move non-interactive uploads behind batched endpoint. Owner: Riley (product).
Week 5–7: scale canary to 25–50% depending on QA; tighten regression alerts and rollback triggers. Owner: Priya + customer success.
Week 7–8: full rollout and cost/savings validation; sign-off for committed Dedicated option if customer opts in. Owner: Account lead + Solutions Eng.

Measurement and gates:
- Primary metric: net monthly inference spend (billing + RW telemetry) with target to meet at least Conservative savings within 30 days of rollout completion.
- Quality gate: no statistically significant drop (>1.5% delta) on the clinical QA set; human escalation for any critical failure.
- Latency gate: 95p should not increase >10% from baseline during rollout.

Appendix: quick topology simulation (sample numbers)

| Line item                     | Baseline ($) | Likely scenario ($) | Notes                         |
|-------------------------------|--------------|---------------------|-------------------------------|
| Generator compute (GPU)       | 150,000      | 72,000              | model routing + quantization  |
| Token processing & overhead   | 45,000       | 28,000              | KV cache + templating         |
| Embeddings                    | 15,000       | 6,550               | batching + aggregation        |
| Total                         | 210,000      | 106,550             | ~54% reduction                |

(Precise numbers use telemetry-derived per-call cost, see linked Confluence page for full spreadsheet with per-route simulation and sensitivity knobs.)

Recommended next steps (short list):
- Approve staged rollout plan and mapping to Mariposa SLAs (Legal/Sec review for KV).
- Run 2-week quantized-vs-fp16 A/B with focused human evaluation set.
- Deliver a small embedded-runner change to enable 100ms aggregation window for non-interactive uploads.
- Re-run full cost-sim workbook with live telemetry after canary to produce an updated committed-savings estimate for Dedicated pricing negotiation.

Notes to reviewer: this doc intentionally conservative on quality-impact assumptions. If Mariposa is willing to accept more aggressive quantization and dedicated capacity commitments we can push to the Aggressive scenario quickly.

Signed-off-by: Priya Nair (product-optimize)
